title: OpenAI-compat: decouple tool scoring propagation and introduce stream boundary markers for deterministic tool handoffs
author: Maya R. Singh
release_notes: OpenAI-compat: improve determinism for streamed tool handoffs by emitting explicit stream boundary markers and decoupling score propagation. Backwards-compatible; telemetry added.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers using the OpenAI compatibility layer reported nondeterministic tool handoffs when responses were streamed and partial fragments contained tool metadata. This manifested as duplicate tool invocations or missing final tool_choice in edge cases (long-running streaming, network retries, and interleaved assistant/tool messages). The goal of this PR is twofold: (1) decouple how tool selection scores are propagated through the pipeline from the streaming framing mechanism, and (2) add explicit stream boundary markers so consumers and intermediate proxies can deterministically recognize handoff points and resume or coalesce fragments safely.

Summary of changes: a) Introduce a dedicated "score propagation" stage in the OpenAI-compat adapter that carries a normalized score_provenance blob alongside the chosen tool id. This makes the semantics: choose -> score_propagate -> emit_tool_frame, which avoids accidental overwrites when streaming fragments are interleaved. b) Add a lightweight stream boundary marker (SSE/fragment token: "X-RW-STREAM-BNDY:v1") that is emitted immediately before and after tool frames in streaming responses. Consumers can use the boundary to coalesce fragments, enforce idempotency, and anchor KV cache resume points. c) Enrich tool frames with an optional deterministic handoff id (handoff_id) and provenance header (tool_score_src) so downstream systems (routing, retries, telemetry) can attribute invocations correctly. d) Backwards-compatible parsing: if consumers do not understand the boundary token, the adapter falls back to existing heuristics and emits a best-effort final tool_call event. e) Tests and docs: unit + integration tests covering fragmented streams, network retry replay, and a short e2e harness against the SDK compat adapter.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (ENG-4218) reviewed - [x] Unit tests for score propagation and parsing - [x] Integration tests for fragment coalescing and resume - [x] Telemetry counters and histograms instrumented - [x] Docs: streaming boundary spec drafted - [x] Backwards compatibility validated with existing OpenAI-compat consumers

Commits (high-level): ["extract: openai_compat.score_propagation stage (core adapter)", "feat: emit stream boundary markers around tool frames (streaming runtime)", "feat: add handoff_id and tool_score_src headers (protocol)", "test: fragmented stream and retry replay tests", "docs: streaming-boundary specification and examples", "chore: update changelog & console notes"]

Files touched (high level): ["runtime/openai_compat/score_propagation.py", "runtime/streaming/stream_markers.go", "api/compat/handler.py", "tests/openai_compat/test_tool_choice_stream.py", "docs/openai-compat/streaming-boundaries.md", "console/release-notes/2.14.md"]

Testing and CI: All automated CI runs passed after the third iteration. The first CI run flagged a race when the streaming goroutine updated the in-memory choice record; fixed by switching to compare-and-swap when promoting provisional scores. Benchmarks: micro-benchmarks show a <1.5% p99 increase in very small synthetic workloads due to extra marker bytes on the wire; real workloads with prefix caching show neutral-to-positive end-to-end latency because the deterministic handoff reduces duplicate tool calls and retries.

Review conversation (high-level, chronological): 
- Jonas Meyer (reviewer): "Design LGTM. Two requests: (1) can we keep the marker byte footprint minimal and make the token opt-in via config? (2) add an invariant test that ensures handoff_id is unique per tool handoff in a stream."
- Maya (author): "Re: marker opt-in: added runtime flag openai.compat.stream_boundary_enabled (default true for cloud, false for private by default) and a command-line override for private deploys. Handoff_id uniqueness test added; used a monotonic counter per request with collision check."
- Priya Kapoor (reviewer): "Please add telemetry events for when we fall back to heuristic parsing (so we can measure compatibility surface). Also call out behaviour in release notes."
- Maya: "Added counters: openai_compat.boundary.unrecognized and openai_compat.handoff.fallback_reason (enum). Documented in release notes with migration guidance."
- Liam O'Connor (approver): "Minor nit: move the stream marker constant to the top-level streaming package so other adapters can reuse it. Otherwise approved."
- Maya: "Moved constant and added a short doc comment referencing the protocol stability guarantees."

Edge cases & compatibility notes: - If a client strips headers or minifies SSE payloads, the handoff_id still appears embedded in the tool frame JSON; the adapter also emits an alignment token so partial reads can re-sync. - For older clients that expect the older openai-compat sequence, the adapter will still emit the final tool_call event and include tool_choice.score in the final JSON so existing consumers remain functional. - The stream boundary marker is intentionally human-readable for easier inspection during incidents but compact (26 bytes). Operators can opt-out in private deployments if they have strict wire policies.

Telemetry and observability: Added counters and histograms: openai_compat.tool_handoff.count, openai_compat.handoff.latency_ms, openai_compat.boundary.unrecognized, openai_compat.handoff.duplicate_detected. Added a per-request trace span "openai.compat.score_propagate" and tags for handoff_id and chosen_tool.

Migration and rollout plan: - Stage 1 (canary): enable flags for internal canaries and Redwood-hosted customers (2 days) - Stage 2 (gradual): default-on for hosted API, opt-in for Dedicated/Private (2 weeks) - Stage 3 (monitor): roll out to all customers after 2 weeks if telemetry stable. Backout: disable stream_boundary_enabled config and return to legacy framing.

Merge outcome: Squash-and-merged after approvals. Changelog entry added to console release notes and public docs.

Why this is different from previous PRs: Instead of trying to infer tool scores from fragmented messages or bundling scoring logic into the streaming emitter, this PR separates concerns: a deterministic score propagation stage followed by an explicit, minimal streaming framing protocol. That reduces accidental state mutation in streaming paths and gives downstream systems a small but reliable contract for tool handoffs.
